meta.title: SIA OSDP machine-readable reference for protocol decoding
meta.source: 78890beb-SIA-OSDP-2.2-2.docx.pdf (87 PDF pages). Cover reads 'OSDP Version 2.2.2', footer 'OSDP v2.2.2, (c)2024 Security Industry Association'.
meta.pageConvention: All 'page' values are the printed page numbers in the page footer ('- N -'). PDF page index = printed page + 1 (the cover is unnumbered).
meta.byteOrder: Multi-byte numbers are little-endian (LSB first) unless a field says otherwise (section 5.5, p.11). Exceptions stated by the spec: PIVDATA object ID (MSB first, p.31) and the Secure PIN Entry fields listed MSB-then-LSB (p.40).
meta.offsetConvention: Field 'offset' is counted from the first DATA byte, i.e. the byte right after the CMND/REPLY code. For record-based messages, 'record' offsets are counted within one record. size 'var' means the size depends on a length field or on the remaining DATA length.
meta.status: Extracted from the spec. Where the spec contradicts itself, the conflict is recorded in 'specIssues' and at the field concerned. Nothing is invented; notes that come from outside the spec are marked 'external'.
meta.verification: Checksum and CRC-16 (init 0x1D0F, poly 0x1021) reproduce all Annex E frame check bytes (incl. the CHLNG and RMAC_I frames); AES session keys, client/server cryptograms and RMAC_I recomputed from SCBK-D/RND.A/RND.B match Annex E exactly.

ctrlBits.name: SQN
ctrlBits.description: Sequence number, used to confirm delivery and to recover from errors. See sequenceRules.

values.0: an 8-bit CHECKSUM is in the last byte of the message
values.1: a 16-bit CRC is in the last 2 bytes of the message
a Security Control Block is present

ctrlBits.name: reserved
ctrlBits.description: Shall be set to 0x00. A non-zero value is a protocol anomaly.

timing.REPLY_DELAY_definition: Time from receipt of the checksum character of the command to transmission of the first byte of the reply. A device shall start its reply in less than REPLY_DELAY.
timing.interCharacterTimeoutNote: Nominal value; may be adjusted for special channel timing. An inter-character timeout while receiving aborts the receive and the PD re-syncs on the next SOM.
timing.lineIdleBeforeTransmit: At least the time of two characters of idle line before a device may access the channel.
timing.markBeforeFirstChar: Drive the line to marking for at least one character time before the first character (for example by sending 0xFF).
timing.releaseAfterLastChar: Stop driving the line no later than one full character time after the stop bit of the last character.
timing.offlineRule: The PD considers communication off-line if more than 8 seconds pass between messages it answers. Both sides then reset the connection state to off-line and start a new connect sequence.
timing.acuNoReply: If the ACU gets no reply within REPLY_DELAY, it moves on to the next communication cycle.
timing.retries: The ACU should retry a limited number of times. 2.2 recommends at most 3 attempts, then restarting the OSDP session. If the PD sends a NAK other than bad checksum, retrying should stop.

securityBlock.handshakeBlocks: For SCS_11..SCS_14, SEC_BLK_LEN = 3 and SEC_BLK_DATA[0] selects the key: 0x01 = SCBK, 0x00 = SCBK-D (default key). In SCS_14, SEC_BLK_DATA[0] = 0x01 means the server cryptogram was accepted and 0xFF means it was rejected (p.78-79).
securityBlock.sessionBlocks: The spec gives no SEC_BLK_DATA content for SCS_15..SCS_18 and does not state their SEC_BLK_LEN explicitly (external: SEC_BLK_LEN=2, no data, in practice).

errorsFromPD.0x05: PD received an SB it does not support
errorsFromPD.0x06: PD needs encryption and got a command without the right security extension

types.name: SCS_15
types.meaning: Secure Session msg. w. MAC, authenticated only or with non-encrypted Data.
types.usage: Meant only for commands with no DATA field. Production implementations should reject a plaintext payload in SCS_15 (p.80).

types.name: SCS_16
types.meaning: Secure Session msg. w. MAC, authenticated only or with non-encrypted Data.
types.usage: Meant only for replies with no DATA field (p.80).

types.name: SCS_17
types.meaning: Secure Session msg. with MAC & Data Encryption
types.usage: Shall be used with every command that has a DATA field; DATA is padded and encrypted with S-ENC (p.80).

types.name: SCS_18
types.meaning: Secure Session msg. with MAC & Data Encryption
types.usage: Shall be used with every reply that has a DATA field (p.80).

commands.name: osdp_POLL
commands.description: General inquiry: asks the PD for any unreported event, input, or status change.
reply: any reply marked as a poll response: osdp_LSTATR, osdp_ISTATR, osdp_OSTATR, osdp_RSTATR, osdp_RAW, osdp_FMT, osdp_KEYPAD, osdp_BIOREADR, osdp_BIOMATCHR, osdp_MFGREP, osdp_XRD, osdp_MFGSTATR, osdp_MFGERRR

commands.name: osdp_ID
commands.description: Asks the PD for its identification report (vendor, model, serial, firmware).

commands.name: osdp_CAP
commands.description: Asks the PD to list its capabilities (inputs, outputs, readers, LEDs, security, and so on).

commands.name: osdp_LSTAT
commands.description: Asks the PD for its local status (enclosure tamper and power).

commands.name: osdp_ISTAT
commands.description: Asks the PD for the state of all its inputs.

commands.name: osdp_OSTAT
commands.description: Asks the PD for the state of all its outputs.

commands.name: osdp_RSTAT
commands.description: Asks the PD for the tamper status of its attached readers.

commands.name: osdp_OUT
commands.description: Sets outputs (such as relays) on or off, permanently or for a timed pulse.
commands.recordNotes: One or more 4-byte records; count = DATA length / 4. There must be at least one. The count should not exceed the number of outputs in PDCAP Function Code 2. An invalid output number or control code gives NAK 0x09.

record.name: Output Number
record.description: 0x00 = first output, 0x01 = second output, and so on.

record.name: Timer
record.description: 16-bit timer in units of 100 ms. 0x0000 means 'forever'.

examples.meaning: Turn off the first and second outputs and turn on the third (set default states).
Turn the second output on for 5 seconds.
Turn the second output on for 5 s and set its permanent state to off.
Turn the third output off for 100 ms and make its permanent state on.

commands.notes: The PD may answer osdp_OSTATR right away, or osdp_ACK and send osdp_OSTATR later as a poll response.

commands.name: osdp_LED
commands.description: Controls reader LEDs, with a temporary (timed, flashing) setting and a permanent setting.
commands.recordNotes: One or more 14-byte records; count = DATA length / 14. An invalid reader or LED number gives NAK 0x09. A new temporary command overrides an active one. ON time and OFF time cannot both be zero. When the temporary timer expires, the LED goes back to the last permanent state. The permanent state is lost on power cycle. The LED alternates between the ON and OFF colours; using the same colour for both gives a steady light. The 16-bit timer applies only to the temporary setting.

record.name: LED Number
record.description: 0x00 = first LED, 0x01 = second LED, and so on.

record.name: Temporary ON Time
record.description: ON duration of the flash. 0x00 means no duration.

record.name: Temporary OFF Time
record.description: OFF duration of the flash. 0x00 means no duration.

record.name: Temporary Timer
record.description: How long the temporary setting lasts. 0x0000 means 'forever'.

record.name: Permanent Control Code
record.description: The mode to return to after the timer expires.

examples.meaning: First LED on the first reader flashes red (100 ms) / black (200 ms) for 3 seconds, then returns to its current display mode.
The reader's second LED shows steady green.

commands.name: osdp_BUZ
commands.description: Controls the reader's single-tone buzzer (tone, on/off timing, repeat count).
commands.notes: An invalid Reader Number gives NAK 0x09. The spec's table gives no reply list; ACK/NAK are the general replies (6.1).

fields.name: On Time
fields.description: ON duration of the sound. Must be non-zero unless the tone code is 0x01 (off).

fields.name: Count
fields.description: Number of times to repeat the ON/OFF cycle. 0x00 means the tone continues until another tone command arrives or the PD reboots.

commands.name: osdp_TEXT
commands.description: Shows a text string on the reader's character display, permanently or temporarily.
commands.notes: Commands to display elements that do not exist get a NAK. Temp text overwrites a field for a time and then the permanent text comes back. For a permanent text command, Temp Text Time has another meaning: 0 = let active temp text finish; non-zero = abort active temp text and show the permanent text now. Permanent text is lost on power cycle. Dates/times should use ISO 8601 GeneralizedTime.

fields.name: Temp Text Time
fields.description: How long temporary text is shown.

fields.name: Row
fields.description: Row of the first character. 0x01 = top row.

fields.name: Column
fields.description: Column of the first character. 0x01 = leftmost column.

fields.name: Text Length
fields.description: Number of characters in the string.

commands.name: osdp_COMSET
commands.description: Changes the PD's address and baud rate; the change takes effect after the PD replies.
commands.notes: The spec's Table 22 points to 'subclause 7.4' for osdp_COM; the correct section is 7.13. If the PD cannot comply, it replies with the values it will actually use. These settings are recommended to be non-volatile.

fields.name: Address
fields.description: Unit ID the PD will answer to after the change.

fields.name: Baud Rate
fields.description: Actual baud rate to use, such as 9600 or 38400.

example.meaning: Broadcast COMSET, SQN 0, CRC: set address 0x00 and baud 0x00002580 = 9600 (from the CRC test vector, p.86).

commands.name: osdp_BIOREAD
commands.description: Tells the reader to take a biometric scan and send the data back later as osdp_BIOREADR.

fields.name: BIO_FORMAT
fields.description: Format of the data to return.

commands.name: osdp_BIOMATCH
commands.description: Tells the reader to scan a biometric and compare it with the template sent in this message; the result comes back as osdp_BIOMATCHR.
commands.notes: If BIO_LENGTH is 0x0000, the PD uses a template it received earlier (for example via osdp_FILETRANSFER type 0x02).

fields.name: BIO_QUALITY
fields.description: Threshold needed to accept the match, normalised.

commands.name: osdp_KEYSET
commands.description: Sends a new Secure Channel Base Key (SCBK) from the ACU to the PD.
commands.notes: Only sent and accepted when the connection is 'secure': either encrypted with keys from the current SCBK/SCBK-D, or physically secure in a special installation setup mode. Devices leave installation mode after a successful KEYSET. Being inside a secure channel means this travels as SCS_17 with the key encrypted.

fields.name: Key_Type
fields.description: Encryption method this key is for.

fields.name: Length
fields.description: Number of key bytes = (key length in bits + 7) / 8. 16 for a 128-bit SCBK.

commands.name: osdp_CHLNG
commands.description: Starts a secure channel session: the ACU sends an 8-byte random challenge (RND.A) with an SCS_11 header.
commands.securityBlock: SCS_11, SEC_BLK_LEN 3, SEC_BLK_DATA[0]: 0x01 = use SCBK, 0x00 = use SCBK-D
commands.notes: A PD that does not support the security block or SCS_11 answers NAK 0x05.

fields.name: Random Number (RND.A)
fields.description: Random number made by the ACU (server challenge).

example.meaning: CHLNG to address 0, SQN 1, CRC+SCB, SCS_11 using SCBK-D, RND.A=B0..B7 (p.86).

commands.name: osdp_SCRYPT
commands.description: Secure channel step 3: the ACU sends its 16-byte server cryptogram so the PD can check the ACU knows the key.
commands.notes: D.2.3 says 'SCS connection sequence value is SCS_12', which conflicts with D.1 and D.1.3.3 (SCS_13). SCS_13 is correct, as the test vector shows.

commands.name: osdp_ACURXSIZE
commands.description: Tells the PD the largest message the ACU can receive.
commands.notes: The spec gives no reply list; ACK/NAK assumed from 6.1.

commands.name: osdp_FILETRANSFER
commands.description: Sends one fragment of a file (firmware, configuration, template, and so on) from the ACU to the PD.
commands.notes: Usually many message/reply pairs. The first fragment uses the default message size (128 bytes) or no more than the PDCAP value. Transfers continue until the PD aborts or the transfer finishes. Offsets must increase. Table 34 says 'DATA (12 bytes)' but the listed header fields add up to 11 bytes.

fields.name: FtOffset
fields.description: Offset in the file of this message's data. Must increase with each message.

commands.name: osdp_MFG
commands.description: A manufacturer-specific command, identified by the vendor's 3-byte IEEE OUI.
commands.notes: The PD reads the 3-byte Vendor Code together with a Command_ID to decide what the command means. Vendors define their own Command_IDs. The spec says 'four bytes formed by the three byte VendorCode and the Command_ID', so the first byte after the vendor code is in effect the Command_ID, although Table 27 only calls it vendor-defined DATA.

fields.name: DATA
fields.description: Vendor defined (starts with the vendor's Command_ID).

commands.name: osdp_XWR
commands.description: Extended Write: smart card / transparent-mode command, identified by the pair (XRW_MODE, XWR_PCMND).

fields.name: XWR_PCMND
fields.description: Command code that depends on XRW_MODE. See subcommands.

fields.name: XWR_PDATA
fields.description: Optional data that depends on XWR_PCMND.

subcommands.name: Mode-00 Read Setting (osdp_PR00REQ)
subcommands.description: Asks the PD for its current background behaviour mode.

subcommands.name: Mode Set
subcommands.description: Sets the background behaviour mode and its configuration.

fields.name: Mode config
fields.description: 0x00 if absent. Mode 0: bit0 1 = enable / 0 = disable the Mode 0 Extended Read Card Info Report response (osdp_PR00CIRR); bits 1-7 are zero. Mode 1: bits 0-7 are zero.

values.0x00: Disable Read Card Info Report Response
values.0x01: Enable Read Card Info Report Response (Mode 0 only)

subcommands.name: Mode-01 Transparent Content Send Request (XMIT)
subcommands.description: Passes an APDU through the reader to the smart card.

fields.name: APDU
fields.description: Valid APDU to send to the smart card.

subcommands.notes: The text mentions '1 byte destination', but Table 41 has no destination field. The card's answer comes later as osdp_PR01SCREP.

subcommands.name: Mode-01 Connection Done
subcommands.description: Tells the reader to end its connection to the smart card.

subcommands.name: Mode-01 Request Secure PIN Entry
subcommands.description: Tells the reader to collect a PIN on its keypad, put it into the supplied APDU, and send that to the card (the PIN never goes over OSDP). The reader should not add these keys to the keypad buffer.
subcommands.notes: The text says a '22-byte header' but Table 43 says 'DATA (20 bytes)', and the fields add up to 20 bytes including XRW_MODE and XWR_PCMND. Structure follows the PC/SC v2.02 Part 10 PIN_VERIFY_STRUCTURE.

fields.name: TimeOut2
fields.description: Timeout after the first key press.

fields.name: PINBlockString
fields.description: Bits 3-0: PIN block size in bytes after justification and formatting. Bits 7-4: bit size of the PIN length in the APDU.

fields.name: PINLengthFormat
fields.description: Bits 3-0: PIN length position in system units. Bit 4: set if system units are bytes, clear if bits. Bits 7-5: reserved.

fields.name: PINMaxExtraDigit
fields.description: XXYY: XX = minimum PIN size in digits, YY = maximum.

fields.name: EntryValidationCondition
fields.description: Conditions under which PIN entry counts as complete.

fields.name: Number Message
fields.description: Number of verification messages to display.

fields.name: DataLength
fields.description: Length of the APDU sent to the card.

fields.name: APDU
fields.description: APDU for the card (the PIN is inserted by the reader).

subcommands.name: Mode-01 Smartcard Scan (osdp_PR01SCSCAN)
subcommands.description: Asks whether a smart card is present at the reader.

commands.name: osdp_ABORT
commands.description: Tells the PD to stop the current operation, including any multi-part message or file transfer in progress.
commands.notes: A PD that cannot abort (for example during a firmware update file transfer) returns osdp_NAK.

commands.name: osdp_PIVDATA
commands.description: Asks the PD to read a selected data object from a PIV card.
commands.notes: Some fields are MSB first to match the card contents. Data offset may change size or be deprecated in 2.3.

fields.name: Data offset
fields.description: Single-byte offset within the requested field. Offsets over one byte are not officially supported in 2.2.

commands.name: osdp_GENAUTH
commands.description: Asks the PD to have a PIV card run a General Authenticate (sends an encrypted challenge and expects a decrypted answer).
commands.notes: Algorithm and Key are only in the first fragment; later fragments leave them out. Table 32 says 'DATA (10 bytes)' but the listed header fields add up to 9 bytes before the challenge. Algorithm is shown as LSB/MSB rows, i.e. 2 bytes.

fields.name: Challenge
fields.description: Fragment of the cryptographic challenge payload.

commands.name: osdp_CRAUTH
commands.description: Asks the PD to run a challenge/response with the card (sends a plaintext challenge and expects an encrypted answer).
commands.notes: Same layout as osdp_GENAUTH. Algorithm and Key are only in the first fragment.

fields.name: Challenge
fields.description: Fragment of the cryptographic challenge payload.

commands.name: osdp_KEEPACTIVE
commands.description: Tells the PD to keep the reader's connection with the credential (card) alive for the given time.
commands.notes: The spec gives no reply list; ACK/NAK assumed.

fields.name: KP_ACT_TIME
fields.description: How long to keep the card connection alive.

replies.name: osdp_ACK
replies.description: The command was accepted and there is nothing else to report.
replies.inResponseTo: any valid command that needs no specific reply; osdp_POLL when there is nothing to report

replies.name: osdp_NAK
replies.description: The command was not processed; the first byte says why.

fields.name: Data
fields.description: Depends on the error code. For 0x09: optional array of one completion code per command record (0x00 = no error, 0xFF = generic error, others reserved). It is left out when the command had one record or when no records were processed because of bad record sizing.

replies.name: osdp_PDID
replies.description: Device identification: vendor, model, version, serial number, and firmware version.
replies.notes: The cUID used by the secure channel is the first 8 bytes of the PDID reply.

fields.name: Model Number
fields.description: Manufacturer's model number (assigned by the vendor).

fields.name: Serial Number
fields.description: 32-bit serial number assigned by the vendor.

replies.name: osdp_PDCAP
replies.description: List of the PD's capabilities, one 3-byte record per function.
replies.notes: Records may come in any order; count = DATA length / 3. A missing function code means it is not supported.

record.name: Compliance
record.description: Compliance level; its meaning depends on the function code (Annex B).

record.name: Number of
record.description: Number of objects of this type; its meaning depends on the function code (Annex B).

replies.name: osdp_LSTATR
replies.description: Local status: enclosure tamper and power supply status.
replies.inResponseTo: osdp_LSTAT, or a poll response when either status has changed

fields.name: Tamper Status
fields.description: Found by monitoring the enclosure tamper mechanism.

fields.name: Power Status
fields.description: Taken from the power supply status.

replies.name: osdp_ISTATR
replies.description: Status of every input, one byte per input.
replies.inResponseTo: osdp_ISTAT, or a poll response when any input changed
replies.notes: The first byte is input 0, the next is input 1, and so on. Every input is reported.

replies.name: osdp_OSTATR
replies.description: Status of every output, one byte per output.
replies.inResponseTo: osdp_OSTAT, osdp_OUT, or a poll response when any output changed
replies.notes: One byte for each output reported in PDCAP Function Code 2, in order.

replies.name: osdp_RSTATR
replies.description: Tamper status of each attached external reader, one byte per reader.
replies.inResponseTo: osdp_RSTAT, or a poll response when any reader status changed
replies.notes: Only applies when an external reader is attached and the PD can monitor it. Table 54 shows 'DATA (1 byte)'; the text says one byte per reader.

replies.name: osdp_RAW
replies.description: Card read: raw card bits (for example Wiegand), not decoded.
replies.inResponseTo: osdp_POLL (poll response) after a card read
replies.notes: Unreported card data is deleted during or after a communication loss. With secure channel, this travels as SCS_18 and the card number is encrypted.

fields.name: Bit Count
fields.description: Number of card bits (the table calls it 'Template length'). The number of data bytes = ceil(BitCount/8) (derived).

fields.name: Data
fields.description: 8 card bits per data byte, MSB to LSB, left justified.

replies.name: osdp_FMT
replies.description: Card read as decoded ASCII characters (deprecated).

fields.name: Character Count
fields.description: Number of characters, including START, END, CKSUM.

replies.name: osdp_KEYPAD
replies.description: Keys pressed on the reader's keypad.
replies.inResponseTo: osdp_POLL (poll response) when the keypad buffer has data
replies.notes: Unreported keypad data is deleted during or after a communication loss. In plaintext (no secure channel) the PIN digits can be read directly.

fields.name: Digit Count
fields.description: Number of keypad digits that follow.

replies.name: osdp_COM
replies.description: The address and baud rate the PD will use after sending this reply.

fields.name: Address
fields.description: Unit ID the PD will answer to.

replies.name: osdp_BIOREADR
replies.description: Result of a biometric scan requested by osdp_BIOREAD.
replies.notes: May be split into several packets because of the template size (multi-part). Table 59 says 'DATA (7 bytes)'; the listed fixed fields are 6 bytes before the template.

replies.name: osdp_BIOMATCHR
replies.description: Whether the scanned biometric matched the template sent in osdp_BIOMATCH.

replies.name: osdp_CCRYPT
replies.description: Secure channel step 2: the PD sends its ID (cUID), its random number (RND.B) and its client cryptogram.
replies.notes: Same code value (0x76) as the osdp_CHLNG command; tell them apart by direction (ADDR bit 0x80). D.3.1 says 'SCS connection sequence value is SCS_13', which conflicts with D.1 and D.1.3.2 (SCS_12). SCS_12 is correct per the test vector.

fields.name: Client ID (cUID)
fields.description: Client's Unique Identifier (the first 8 bytes of PDID).

fields.name: Random Number (RND.B)
fields.description: Random number made by the PD.

example.meaning: CCRYPT reply from address 0 (0x80), SQN 1, SCS_12 with SCBK-D (p.86). Spacing as printed in the spec. The cUID segment as printed ('00 68E0000000000') is only 7.5 bytes, a typo in the spec.

replies.name: osdp_RMAC_I
replies.description: Secure channel step 4: the PD accepts the ACU's cryptogram and sends the initial MAC that starts the rolling MAC chain.
replies.securityBlock: SCS_14, SEC_BLK_DATA[0]: 0x01 = server cryptogram accepted, 0xFF = server cryptogram rejected (secure channel cannot continue)

fields.name: MAC_I
fields.description: Initial R-MAC = AES-ENC(AES-ENC(ServerCryptogram, S-MAC1), S-MAC2). This is the first ICV for the session.

replies.name: osdp_BUSY
replies.description: The PD is busy and cannot handle the command now; the ACU should send the same command again.
replies.notes: SQN is always 0. Always sent outside the secure channel (plain checksum/CRC, no SCB) and does not affect the secured messages before or after it. The ACU repeats the command in its original form until it gets something other than BUSY, or gives up; if it gives up, the new sequence number tells the PD to process the new command.

replies.name: osdp_FTSTAT
replies.description: File transfer status: whether to continue, wait, or stop, and flow-control hints.
replies.codeConflict: Table 68 prints the code as 0x84 (which is osdp_MFGERRR). Annex A (normative, Table A.2) gives 0x7A. Decode as 0x7A.

fields.name: FtDelay
fields.description: Delay the ACU should wait before the next osdp_FILETRANSFER. 0 = no delay needed.

fields.name: FtUpdateMsgMax
fields.description: Alternative maximum message size for later FILETRANSFER messages. 0 = no change requested; otherwise use it as the maximum FtFragmentSize in the next message. It may change from message to message.

replies.name: osdp_PIVDATAR
replies.description: Data read from a PIV card, sent in fragments.
replies.notes: Same code value (0x80) as the osdp_MFG command; tell them apart by direction.

replies.name: osdp_GENAUTHR
replies.description: The card's answer to General Authenticate, sent in fragments.

replies.name: osdp_CRAUTHR
replies.description: The card's answer to a challenge/response request, sent in fragments.

replies.name: osdp_MFGSTATR
replies.description: Manufacturer-specific status (deprecated; to be redefined in 2.3.0).
replies.inResponseTo: sent when a status condition needs a manufacturer-specific reply

replies.name: osdp_MFGERRR
replies.description: Manufacturer-specific error (deprecated; to be redefined in 2.3.0).
replies.inResponseTo: sent when an error condition needs a manufacturer-specific reply

replies.name: osdp_MFGREP
replies.description: A manufacturer-specific reply, identified by the vendor's 3-byte IEEE OUI.
replies.notes: Table 61 describes the Data as 'Keypad data represented as ASCII characters', a copy-paste error; the content is vendor defined.

replies.name: osdp_XRD
replies.description: Extended Read: smart card / transparent-mode reply, identified by the pair (XRW_MODE, XRD_REPLY).
replies.notes: Table 69 labels the third field 'XRW_MODE'; it is the optional reply data (XRD_PDATA). The spec uses the names XRD_REPLY and XRD_PREPLY for the same thing.

fields.name: XRD_REPLY
fields.description: Reply code that depends on XRW_MODE (Table 70 for mode 0, Table 74 for mode 1).

fields.name: XRD_PDATA
fields.description: Optional data that depends on the reply.

subreplies.name: osdp_PR00ERROR
subreplies.description: Mode 0 error or NAK: the PD could not process a Mode 0 command.

fields.name: Error Code
fields.description: Transparent mode error condition (values are not defined by the spec).

subreplies.name: osdp_PR00REQR
subreplies.description: Current background behaviour mode and configuration (answer to Mode-00 Read Setting).

subreplies.name: osdp_PR00CIRR
subreplies.description: Card information report: a smart card was detected (poll response, when enabled with Mode Set config bit 0).

fields.name: Length of CSN
fields.description: Byte size of the CSN (0 = no data).

subreplies.name: osdp_PR01ERROR
subreplies.description: Mode 1 error or NAK for any Mode 1 command, or a poll response.

subreplies.name: osdp_PR01PRES
subreplies.description: Card present notification: answer to Smartcard Scan (PR01SCSCAN), or a poll response.

fields.name: Status
fields.description: Smart card present status (the spec says 'Refer to table 73'; the values are in Table 74).

subreplies.note: Table 76 prints XRD_PREPLY = 0x00 with the text 'error report', which is the same as PR01ERROR. This looks like a copy error. (External: earlier OSDP versions and common implementations use 0x01 for PR01PRES.)

subreplies.preply: not clearly stated (Table 77 prints XRW_PCMND 0x03 'Secure PIN Entry Request', a copy error)
subreplies.name: osdp_PR01SCREP
subreplies.description: Transparent card data: the smart card's answer APDU to an XMIT (XWR mode 1, PCMND 0x01).

fields.name: APDU

pdcapFunctionCodes.recordLayout: Byte 0 Function Code | Byte 1 Compliance (level of compliance with the function) | Byte 2 Number of (number of objects of this type)

1.name: Contact Status Monitoring
1.description: Can monitor the state of a switch through a two-wire connection (inputs).

compliance.0x01: PD monitors and reports the state of the circuit without any supervision, using its default interpretation of contact state as active/inactive.
compliance.0x02: Like 01, plus: the open/closed to active/inactive encoding can be configured (normally closed / normally open).
compliance.0x03: Like 02, plus: supervised monitoring; each circuit's operating mode is set by configuration.
compliance.0x04: Like 03, plus: custom End-Of-Line settings within the manufacturer's guidelines.

2.name: Output Control
2.description: Switched outputs, typically relays, with active/inactive states and optional timed activation.

compliance.0x01: The PD can activate and deactivate the Output on direct command from the ACU.
compliance.0x02: Like 0x01, plus: the Output driver can be configured to set the inactive state (inverted drive, for fail-safe/fail-secure).
compliance.0x03: Like 0x01, plus: timed commands to the Output are accepted.
compliance.0x04: Like 02 and 03 - normal/inverted drive and timed operation.

3.name: Card Data Format
3.description: Form in which card data is sent to the ACU.

compliance.0x01: Card data sent as an array of bits, not exceeding 1024 bits.
compliance.0x02: Card data sent as an array of BCD characters, not exceeding 256 characters.
compliance.0x03: Card data can be sent as an array of bits or as an array of BCD characters.

4.name: Reader LED Control
4.description: Presence and type of reader LEDs.

compliance.0x01: On/off control only; osdp_LED colour values 0-1.
compliance.0x03: Like 02, plus red-green LEDs; colour values 0-2.
compliance.0x04: Like 02, plus red-green-amber LEDs; colour values 0-3.
compliance.0x05: Like 02, plus red-green-blue LEDs; colour values 0-7.
compliance.0x06: Like 02, plus red-green-blue LEDs; may support any colour values 0-255.

4.numberOf: The number of LEDs per reader.

5.name: Reader Audible Output
5.description: Presence and type of a buzzer or tone generator.
5.numberOf: Ignored; there is only one audible output per PD (6.11).

6.name: Reader Text Output
6.numberOf: Number of textual displays per reader.

behaviors.rule: The PD must start its reply less than REPLY_DELAY (at most 200 ms, typically under 3 ms) after the last byte of the command.
behaviors.anomaly: Replies later than 200 ms after the command ends; frequent replies over a few ms may mean an overloaded PD.

behaviors.rule: Only the ACU sends spontaneously. Each command addressed to a PD gets exactly one reply from that PD.
behaviors.anomaly: An unsolicited PD frame, two replies to one command, or a reply from a PD that was not addressed.

behaviors.rule: Reply ADDR = command ADDR | 0x80 (broadcast 0x7F -> 0xFF). Commands have bit 7 clear.
behaviors.anomaly: Reply address does not match the command address; a command with bit 0x80 set; addresses above 0x7F in commands.

behaviors.rule: Address 0x7F should only be used when a single PD is connected.
behaviors.anomaly: Broadcast on a multi-PD bus (possible reply collisions).

behaviors.rule: If no reply arrives within REPLY_DELAY, the ACU moves on to the next communication cycle.
behaviors.anomaly: A timeout.

behaviors.rule: After a timeout, the ACU should resend with the same SQN a limited number of times (recommended at most 3), then restart the session (SQN 0). Retries should stop if the PD sends a NAK other than bad checksum.
behaviors.anomaly: More than 3 consecutive retransmissions; retries continuing after a non-0x01 NAK.

behaviors.rule: The ACU SQN goes 1,2,3,1,2,3... per PD (0 only at startup/reset).
behaviors.anomaly: Skipped SQN values, or SQN 0 in the middle of a session (a reset).

behaviors.rule: A command repeated with the same SQN is a retransmission: the PD should send its previous reply again without running the command a second time. The ACU also does this after receiving a reply with a bad checksum/CRC.

SQN 0 from the ACU means (re)start: the PD discards its last reply and processes the command. A PD reply with SQN 0 (except BUSY) asks the ACU to reset the sequence and clears any secure channel session.
behaviors.anomaly: An unexpected SQN 0 reply means a PD reset or loss of the secure session.

behaviors.rule: NAK 0x04 = unexpected sequence number.
behaviors.anomaly: Sequence desync.

behaviors.rule: After NAK 0x01 (bad checksum/CRC), the ACU may resend. After other NAKs, the ACU should not retry the same command. NAK 0x05/0x06 point to security mismatches; NAK 0x06 on SQN 0 in a session means the PD reset the secure channel; NAK 0x03 means the command is not supported; NAK 0x09 means bad record(s) and may list per-record codes.
behaviors.anomaly: Repeated identical commands after a non-0x01 NAK; a burst of NAK 0x06.

behaviors.rule: osdp_BUSY (SQN 0, never inside the secure channel) means 'try again'. The ACU repeats the same command in its original form (same SQN), right away or after serving other PDs, until it gets a non-BUSY reply, or gives up and moves on with a new SQN, which the PD must treat as a new command.
behaviors.anomaly: BUSY with a non-zero SQN or with an SCB; a long run of BUSY replies.

behaviors.rule: Data that is not available right away: the PD ACKs the command and later returns the data reply to osdp_POLL (for example BIOREAD -> ACK, ... POLL -> BIOREADR). If a specific reply is required and the data is late, the PD answers BUSY.
behaviors.decode: Link a later poll response to the earlier request.

behaviors.rule: Replies allowed to POLL: ACK (nothing to report), LSTATR/ISTATR/OSTATR/RSTATR (on change), RAW/FMT (card read), KEYPAD, BIOREADR, BIOMATCHR, MFGREP, XRD. Card and keypad data not yet reported is deleted on communication loss.
behaviors.anomaly: PDID, PDCAP, COM, CCRYPT or RMAC_I sent in reply to POLL.

behaviors.rule: ID->PDID; CAP->PDCAP; LSTAT->LSTATR; ISTAT->ISTATR; OSTAT->OSTATR; RSTAT->RSTATR; OUT->ACK/OSTATR; LED/BUZ/TEXT/BIOREAD/BIOMATCH/KEYSET/ACURXSIZE/KEEPACTIVE/ABORT->ACK; COMSET->COM; CHLNG->CCRYPT; SCRYPT->RMAC_I; FILETRANSFER->FTSTAT; MFG->ACK/MFGREP; XWR->ACK/XRD; PIVDATA->PIVDATAR; GENAUTH->GENAUTHR; CRAUTH->CRAUTHR. NAK or BUSY is possible for any command.
behaviors.anomaly: A reply code outside the expected set.

behaviors.rule: The PD goes off-line if more than 8 s pass between messages it answers. Both sides reset and restart the connect sequence (SQN 0, and a new secure channel handshake if used).
behaviors.anomaly: More than 8 s gap to a PD, followed by SQN 0 / CHLNG.

behaviors.rule: A gap of more than about 20 ms inside a frame aborts reception; receivers re-sync on the next SOM after an inter-character timeout.
behaviors.anomaly: Gaps inside a frame, or bytes between frames that are not a SOM (noise or a collision).

behaviors.rule: LEN must equal the actual frame length (7-1440). CTRL bits 4-7 must be 0. The check bytes must match (checksum or CRC per CTRL bit 2). A bad check makes the PD answer NAK 0x01.
behaviors.anomaly: LEN mismatch, reserved CTRL bits set, bad CRC/checksum.

behaviors.rule: A PD may reject a frame larger than its RX buffer (PDCAP FC10) with NAK 0x02. All must accept 128 bytes.
behaviors.anomaly: Frames over the PD's advertised buffer.

behaviors.rule: OUT (4-byte records) and LED (14-byte records): DATA length must be a multiple of the record size. If not, NAK 0x09 with no completion array. Records are processed in order; any failure gives NAK 0x09 plus one completion byte per record.
behaviors.anomaly: DATA length not a multiple of the record size.

behaviors.rule: Fragments go in order with no gaps and start at offset 0. The ACU may not interleave other commands to the same PD during a multi-part command, except ABORT. Early end: offset >= total with fragment size 0. The PD may reject with NAK 0x09.
behaviors.anomaly: Offset gaps or going backwards, a first fragment with non-zero offset, other commands to the same PD in the middle of a transfer.

behaviors.rule: FILETRANSFER (first fragment no more than 128 bytes or the PDCAP limit) -> FTSTAT. Status 0 = continue; honour FtDelay ms before the next fragment; FtUpdateMsgMax may raise the fragment size; offsets increase. Status 1 = processed; 2 = PD rebooting (expect full comms reset: SQN 0, re-handshake); 3 = finishing, so the ACU sends idle FILETRANSFERs (size = total, offset = total, fragment size 0) until the status changes; negative = abort/error (-1 abort, -2 unrecognised, -3 malformed). FtAction bit0 = interleave allowed, bit1 = leave secure channel for the transfer, bit2 = a separate poll response is waiting.
behaviors.anomaly: Next fragment sent before FtDelay passed; continuing after a negative status; non-increasing offsets; interleaving when bit0=0.

behaviors.rule: osdp_ABORT ends any multi-part or file transfer in progress. A PD that cannot abort (for example mid firmware update) NAKs.
New address and baud take effect after the PD sends osdp_COM. Expect later traffic at the new address/baud, and the ACU to follow.
behaviors.anomaly: Unexpected COMSET (reconfiguration or hijack attempt).

behaviors.rule: CHLNG(SCS_11) -> CCRYPT(SCS_12) -> SCRYPT(SCS_13) -> RMAC_I(SCS_14), then only SCS_15-18 (plus BUSY / NAK). CTRL SCB bit set on all of them.
behaviors.anomaly: Steps out of order; plaintext (no SCB) commands or replies after the session starts (which ends the session); RMAC_I status 0xFF; repeated handshakes; SCBK-D (SEC_BLK_DATA[0]=0) used outside installation.

behaviors.rule: SCS_15/16 are meant for messages without DATA. Messages with DATA must use SCS_17/18.
behaviors.anomaly: An SCS_15/16 frame that carries DATA (plaintext payload inside a session).

behaviors.rule: KEYSET only over a secure (encrypted) connection or in physically secured installation mode.
behaviors.anomaly: osdp_KEYSET sent in plaintext (the key is exposed) or under SCBK-D.

behaviors.rule: A MAC mismatch (correct CRC, wrong MAC) ends the session. Expect a NAK 0x06 on SQN 0 or a new CHLNG.
behaviors.anomaly: Sessions torn down repeatedly (possible tampering or replay).

behaviors.rule: Codes 0x76 and 0x80 are used in both directions: 0x76 = osdp_CHLNG command / osdp_CCRYPT reply; 0x80 = osdp_MFG command / osdp_PIVDATAR reply. Decode by the ADDR reply bit.
behaviors.decode: Always pick the name from the direction.

behaviors.rule: Command/reply codes not in Annex A are reserved. Vendor extensions must use MFG (0x80) and MFGREP/MFGSTATR/MFGERRR.
behaviors.anomaly: Unknown codes (the PD should NAK 0x03).

secureChannelSteps.carries: SEC_BLK_DATA[0] key select (1=SCBK, 0=SCBK-D); 8-byte RND.A challenge in clear
secureChannelSteps.plain: The ACU asks the reader to start a secure session and sends a random challenge.

secureChannelSteps.carries: Key select; cUID(8) | RND.B(8) | Client Cryptogram(16), all in clear
secureChannelSteps.plain: The reader sends its ID, its own random number, and proof that it knows the shared key. The PD has now derived S-ENC, S-MAC1, S-MAC2. If the ACU sees the PD used a different key (SCBK vs SCBK-D), it may switch keys or restart at SCS_11.

secureChannelSteps.carries: Key select; Server Cryptogram(16) in clear
secureChannelSteps.plain: The ACU checked the reader's proof and now proves that it also knows the key.
The reader accepts (or rejects) the ACU and sends the starting value for the message-authentication chain. On success the session is up. The PD may instead answer NAK 0x05.
